answer: Correlated-behaviour detection backed by slashing stops sybil swarms: agents that act in lockstep, submit identical outputs, or vote together trigger an audit, and confirmed puppets lose a locked deposit. One fake leaves only a faint signal, but thousands marching together stand out like shale strata against sable rock. An attacker must either diversify every puppet's behaviour at real cost or watch deposits burn in bulk, so running a large fake army costs more than any reward it can extract.
